crime: Every night at nine, a prisoner walked the halls, and whenever she found a girl alone, she sat down beside her and drew an ink sun on the back of her hand. By morning it was always gone.

{WITCH_NAME} said yes to everything the prisoners asked of her, then split off another of herself to go and do it. Only the girl with the suns had ever seen two of her at once. On the few nights she happened to be alone when that girl passed, she kept the marked hand out of the water until the sun faded on its own.
At supper in the dining hall, the girl laughed and told her, "There's enough of you for everyone. I'll keep my suns for girls who have nobody."

When {WITCH_NAME} was small, her foster mother sat each night on the bed of whichever child was crying. She herself did every chore she was asked, never cried, and listened to the singing through the wall.

At nine, she stayed at the supper table among the girls and sent one of herself to sit alone at the upper railing. The girl found her there, sat beside her and drew a sun on her hand, though she knew the rest of her was sitting at the table. As the girl stood to go on to the next one, {WITCH_NAME} took her by the legs and tipped her headfirst over the railing onto the path below.
In the trial court, the prisoners ruled that the girl had fallen alone from the railing on her round. From the time the girl set out until she was found, {WITCH_NAME} never left the supper table.

Then one prisoner noticed an ink sun on the back of {WITCH_NAME}'s hand, not yet washed away, though at nine she had been sitting among them. When she let her other self at the railing go, it folded back into her, and its sun came with it. The prisoners understood then that the girl had not fallen alone: one of {WITCH_NAME} had been sitting beside her.
fields.epitaph: There was only ever one girl with the suns, and now there is none of her for any girl left alone.
fields.epithet: Enough for Everyone, Sat With by No One
execution: She is chained to a post inside a ring of iron girls cast in her likeness, each one facing outward toward a different spectator. The iron girls turn inward and close in from every side until their shoulders press her against the post, and there they hold. Then they step back and turn outward again, each to a different spectator. She hangs still at the post, with no one facing her.

magic.name: Plenty of Me
magic.text: She can split into several complete copies of herself, each in a different place at once.
